findings.title: Windows FILE_UPDATE sanitization only strips '/', so backslash ..\ escapes shared/ for arbitrary SYSTEM file write
findings.description: When a Windows agent receives an authenticated FILE_UPDATE control message, receiver-win.c replaces '/' with '-' and flips a leading '.', then fopen(SHAREDCFG_DIR/name, "w"). Backslash is not sanitized. On Windows, fopen treats '\' as a path separator, so names such as ..\ossec.conf or ..\..\..\Users\Public\evil.exe resolve outside shared/. The attacker also controls the declared MD5 and the following payload bytes, so the close-path MD5 check passes. This is distinct from the already-reported UnmergeFiles member-name traversal: prior analysis assumed FILE_UPDATE name sanitization was sufficient for the download path; the '/' -only filter is bypassed with '\' before UnmergeFiles is ever involved. Linux agents are unaffected ('\' is not a separator).
findings.impact: An attacker who can impersonate the manager to a Windows agent (stolen/enrolled agent key, or MITM after key theft) can write arbitrary files as LocalSystem — overwrite ossec.conf, plant autoruns under Users\Public / startup locations, or replace agent binaries — fully compromising the endpoint and disabling HIDS.
findings.attack_path:
1. Attacker obtains a Windows agent key (compromised endpoint, open authd enrollment, or prior key theft).
2. Attacker speaks the secure channel as the manager (UDP/TCP 1514) and sends a control frame: #!-up file <md5> ..\ossec.conf\n (or deeper ..\ chains).
3. receiver-win.c leaves backslashes intact; fopen("shared/..\\ossec.conf") opens the agent install's ossec.conf (ntpath resolves to the agent root).
4. Attacker sends payload frames (non-header) that fprintf into that FILE*.
5. Attacker sends #!-close file ; OS_MD5_File matches the attacker-supplied sum; the written file is kept (basename is not merged.mg, so UnmergeFiles is skipped).
6. Agent now runs attacker-controlled config/binary content as LocalSystem.
findings.remediation: Reject FILE_UPDATE names containing '\\', '/', '..', or drive prefixes. Allowlist [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ and write only basename under SHAREDCFG_DIR. Prefer open() with O_NOFOLLOW on a directory fd. Apply the same checks on Linux for defense in depth.
findings.poc_video_notes: No Windows agent lab in this environment. Confirmed by reading the '/' -only sanitization and simulating ntpath.normpath('shared/..\\ossec.conf') -> 'ossec.conf' and deeper chains to Users\\Public.

excluded_known: Blowfish static IV (no new distinct attack beyond replay)
